intervals.label: assembly at SNOLAB
intervals.note: Start: SNOLAB's page says MiniCLEAN 'began operating at SNOLAB in 2013'; no run before 2017 is documented in the sources read, so 2013 is read as the start of its presence/assembly underground (not verified). End: the first source (March 2014) saying the detector is in final assembly and commissioning ('Assembly of the experiment is underway at SNOLAB').
intervals.quote: MiniCLEAN began operating at SNOLAB in 2013 and began decommissioning in 2019.

intervals.label: final assembly, commissioning and cold-gas run
intervals.note: Only a cold argon gas run (February-April 2017, 18.4 live days) is documented; no source read reports a liquid-argon dark matter run. 2014 sources expected cooling and liquefaction from summer 2014 (arXiv:1403.4842, Sec. 3); the 2017 papers still describe the detector as in commissioning. End: SNOLAB says decommissioning began in 2019.
intervals.quote: The MiniCLEAN detector is undergoing finally assembly and commissioning at the SNOLAB facility in Sudbury, Canada.

summary.plain: MiniCLEAN was a 500 kg detector of liquid argon (or liquid neon) in the Cube Hall at SNOLAB, Canada, built to test a simple single-phase way of hunting for WIMP dark matter. A cold-gas test run took place in 2017 and SNOLAB reports decommissioning began in 2019. No dark matter result was published.
summary.technical: Single-phase liquid argon/neon scintillation detector: 92 cryogenic PMTs with nearly 4pi coverage of a 500 kg (150 kg fiducial) target in a stainless-steel inner vessel, inside a vacuum outer vessel and a water shield tank with a 48-PMT muon veto in the SNOLAB Cube Hall. Pulse-shape discrimination separates nuclear recoils from 39Ar beta events; a 39Ar spike was planned to demonstrate its reach. Prototype for a multi-tonne CLEAN detector. Only a cold-gas run (February-April 2017) is documented; it gave a triplet lifetime of 3.480 us in gaseous argon. No WIMP-search result is published.

technology.quote: The MiniCLEAN dark matter experiment will exploit a single-phase liquid-argon detector instrumented with 92 photomultiplier tubes placed in the cryogen temperature with 4-$\pi$ coverage of a 500 kg (150 kg) target (fiducial) mass.
